These published guidelines explain how to request a verified reporting route and what a useful report should contain once that route is established.

REPORTING CHANNEL NOT CONFIGURED

Dedicated disclosure channel not configured.

Do not submit sensitive vulnerability evidence through general enquiry. No dedicated security email or secure submission endpoint has been confirmed for this website.

Use the contact page only to prepare a non-sensitive request for a verified disclosure channel. If contact delivery is not configured, the page produces a local draft and does not send it.

Request a verified channel — no secrets

Scope & authorization

A formal vulnerability disclosure program, approved target list, and testing rules have not been confirmed. A website being publicly accessible does not grant testing permission. Third-party systems, customer environments, and infrastructure are not authorized targets under these guidelines.

For a concern observed without active testing, first request a verified channel. Any proposed testing requires separate written authorization from the relevant system owner, an agreed scope, and stop conditions.

How to report

  1. Prepare a non-sensitive request for the team’s verified security reporting channel.
  2. Confirm the recipient, secure transfer method, and reporting instructions before sharing evidence.
  3. Send only the minimum evidence needed through that verified route. Keep credentials, personal information, and customer data out of general enquiry.

Do not continue testing, access other users’ data, disrupt services, or attempt persistence while awaiting a response.

Information for a verified report

Once a secure route is agreed, a useful report can include:

  • The affected asset and why you believe it is within the owner’s control.
  • A concise description of the issue, observed impact, and limitations.
  • Minimal reproduction context from already authorized activity or passive observation.
  • Redacted evidence and relevant observation times.
  • A preferred reply route and any handling constraints.

Do not create additional impact to demonstrate severity. Ask the owner how sensitive artifacts should be handled.

What happens next

The owner must confirm channel access, scope, handling instructions, and a review process. Acknowledgment targets, remediation timelines, rewards, and coordinated publication arrangements are not established here.

Request those expectations directly through the verified channel. The website does not represent a bounty program or guarantee a response or fix.

Safe harbor status

These guidelines do not grant permission to test and do not provide a safe harbor promise. A formal safe harbor commitment requires explicit owner approval and an approved program with defined boundaries.

No immunity, legal protection, waiver, or authorization for third-party systems is offered by this notice. Agree any assessment permissions separately before acting.

Contact channel

The general enquiry page is suitable only for asking how to contact the security owner without disclosing vulnerability details. Check its delivery status; a local downloaded draft is not a submitted report.
